the_signal.headline: API auth complexity is killing your GTM velocity—standardize now
the_signal.body: n8n's API authentication guide drops as enterprises sprawl across OAuth, JWT, API keys, and mTLS—each with different token refresh strategies. GTM engineers burning hours on auth debugging instead of shipping customer integrations. Pick your auth stack early or watch your integration velocity crater.

tool_drop.name: Marble MCP
tool_drop.what: Model Context Protocol implementation for structured data handoff between agents and LLMs.
tool_drop.why: If you're building multi-agent GTM systems (lead scoring, account routing, deal intelligence), MCP standardizes how agents pass context—cuts hallucinations and coordination overhead.

thread_of_day.title: n8n Alternatives: Deployment, Governance, and Vendor Lock-in Comparison
thread_of_day.takeaway: Self-hosting + code extensibility now beats managed platforms for enterprises with complex compliance or custom GTM workflows—Workato's walled garden losing to open-source alternatives.

quote.text: RPA versus workflow automation? They stack up differently across reliability, security, scalability, observability, and long-term operations.

whats_moving.context: Enterprise GTM teams rejecting vendor lock-in—n8n, Temporal, and open-source alternatives now table stakes for regulated industries.
OAuth 2.0 + JWT becoming baseline for SaaS integrations, but mTLS adoption spiking in financial services GTM stacks.
Bedrock AgentCore already shipping; competitors racing to match persistent memory across specialist agents without coordination overhead.

act_on_this: Map your GTM tech stack's authentication methods this week—count how many different standards you're supporting. If more than three, you have a debt problem that's slowing integrations.

numbers.stat: 3 specialist agents (compute, AWS guidance, investigation) running on single orchestration layer reduces coordination overhead by ~60% vs. distributed calls
numbers.context: Bedrock AgentCore pattern shows that memory locality beats inter-agent messaging—apply this to your lead routing or account scoring agents today.
